title: Understanding salvation
introduction: Start here to understand why we need salvation, what Jesus Christ has done, and how to respond to Him. Read at your own pace; there is no completion requirement.

sections.title: Why we need salvation
sections.note: Paul says all people have sinned and shows how God makes sinners right with Him through faith in Jesus Christ.
sections.body:
Sin is more than an occasional mistake. We have failed to love and obey God. Paul says that all have sinned and fall short of God’s glory. Religious practice, good behaviour, and comparison with others cannot make us right with Him. We all need salvation.

Romans 3 does not leave us with our guilt. God offers justification by His grace through Jesus Christ, received by faith. Acknowledge your sin honestly, then look at what God has provided rather than trying to make yourself acceptable to Him. If you have questions, write one down to discuss with a trusted Christian or pastor.
sections.prayer: God, help me see my sin honestly and understand the salvation You offer through Jesus Christ.
questions: What does this passage say about why everyone needs salvation?
How does God’s provision differ from trying to earn His acceptance?

sections.title: What Jesus has done
sections.note: The gospel rests on what happened to Jesus: He died for our sins, was buried, and rose again.
sections.body:
Jesus is more than an inspiring example. He died for our sins, was buried, and rose again, just as the gospel Paul received and preached declares. God showed His love while we were still sinners. We cannot save ourselves; our hope rests on the risen Saviour and what He has done.

Name what each passage says about Jesus’ death and resurrection. You do not have to manufacture a powerful feeling to take this good news seriously. Bring your questions honestly and keep examining the testimony about Him.
sections.prayer: God, thank You for sending Jesus to die for sinners and rise again. Help me understand and trust what He has done.
questions: Why are both the cross and the resurrection essential to the gospel?
What are you learning about God’s love for people who have sinned?

sections.title: Repent and accept Jesus Christ
sections.note: Paul calls people to repentance toward God and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. Salvation is God’s gift of grace, received through faith.
sections.body:
Repentance means turning from sin toward God. Accepting Jesus Christ as Lord and Saviour means personally trusting the risen Christ for salvation and acknowledging His rightful place in your life. Romans 10 speaks of confessing Jesus as Lord and believing that God raised Him from the dead. Knowing facts about Jesus, growing up in a Christian family, attending church, or being baptized cannot take the place of this personal response.

Salvation is by grace through faith, not a reward for good works or for already living a perfect life. If you are ready, repent and accept Jesus Christ as your Lord and Saviour, trusting His death for your sins and His resurrection. You may express your faith in your own words; a particular prayer or finishing this reading does not save you. Jesus saves. If you are unsure, bring your questions to a trusted pastor.
sections.prayer: God, I have sinned against You and cannot save myself. I repent and accept Jesus Christ as my Lord and Saviour. I trust His death for my sins and His resurrection for my salvation. Thank You for Your grace.
questions: What is the difference between knowing about Jesus and accepting Him as Lord and Saviour?
Are you relying on Christ or on something you have done to make yourself acceptable to God?

sections.title: A new beginning, not a finish line
sections.note: John connects assurance with God’s testimony about His Son. Acts shows believers beginning a shared life of learning and fellowship.
sections.body:
For those who have repented and accepted Jesus Christ as Lord and Saviour, assurance rests in God’s promise concerning His Son, not in a feeling or a reading record. Growth will involve learning, questions, obedience, and continued repentance when you fail. Jesus, not your performance, is the foundation of your new life.

If you have accepted Christ, tell a trusted Christian and ask for help finding a Bible-teaching local church. Discuss believer’s baptism as a step of obedience after salvation, not a way to obtain it. Begin a small daily reading habit and keep asking questions; you do not need to understand everything today.
sections.prayer: Father, help me rest in Your promise about Jesus. Lead me into a life of learning, obedience, and fellowship with other believers.
questions: Where does John direct a believer’s confidence?
Who could help you take your next step in following Jesus?
